audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Theorem 5.2's nonuniform pairwise hitting times and inverse-rate assignment are inconsistent; The directed Ising rates printed in Section5.2 do not preserve the Gibbs measure; Lemma9.10's pointwise harmonicity domain includes regular-strip boundary with nonzero flux
limitations: Theorem 5.2's nonuniform pairwise hitting times and inverse-rate assignment are inconsistent — Counterevidence: Equal off-diagonal rates do have pairwise mean equal to reciprocal rate. This covers the principal uniform-rate cyclic setting and supplies no contradiction there. The all-other-states exit mean alone matches the asserted total rate.

The directed Ising rates printed in Section5.2 do not preserve the Gibbs measure — Counterevidence: p=0,1 satisfy global balance by translation; p=1/2 satisfies detailed balance. Reference[19] supports pure NE/SW rates; its exponential interpolation(2.30) is one-dimensional. A convex mixture of endpoint rates would be Gibbs-stationary but defines a different process. Usual heat-bath and exponential-half-energy rates differ.

Lemma9.10's pointwise harmonicity domain includes regular-strip boundary with nonzero flux — Counterevidence: Lemma9.9 correctly provides aggregate cancellation, not pointwise zero; p.56 already invokes it with Lemma9.5's potential flatness.

Ground-state quantifiers and projected graph identities need excluded inputs — Counterevidence: Inter-well context and Definition8.1 indicate intended distinct labels; proof and use of Proposition6.21 treat uncollapsed graph vertices outside N(a).

Equation(D.8) has the target-set size instead of the trace-state-space size — Counterevidence: A further trace on A union B would permit that multiplier but is not the trace defined on p.74. Correct |Z| remains spin-label independent; the later path bound e0<2 uses original Dirichlet form independently of(D.8).

Arbitrary path indices, MH energy bound and gateway restriction require local corrections — Counterevidence: Replacing indices byN restores threshold existence; MH conductance uses maximum endpoint energy and supplies intended O(exp(-Gamma beta)) bound; crossing remainder is O(exp(-(Gamma+1)beta)) at fixed volume. AppendixC explicitly not needed in the current paper.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: Theorem 5.2's nonuniform pairwise hitting times and inverse-rate assignment are inconsistent

q=4; p=1/2; periodic torus with 11<=K<L=K+1. Choose sufficiently large fixed K from the asserted prefactor asymptotics, then beta->infinity. kappa1=kappa3=u>0, kappa2=v>0; stated rate to adjacent spins 1/u, opposite spin1/v. Original accelerated hitting time dominates trace hitting time pathwise.

Recorded check: The directed Ising rates printed in Section5.2 do not preserve the Gibbs measure

q=2 encoded as +/-1; K=11,L=12 periodic torus; unordered disagreement Hamiltonian. All positive spins except negative sites (4,5),(5,5),(5,6),(6,5). Printed c_p=exp[-beta(p A+(1-p)B)] with A=NE energy increment,B=SW increment. Any beta>0 and0<p<1,p!=1/2; explicit rational check p=1/3,beta=3log2.

Recorded check: Lemma9.10's pointwise harmonicity domain includes regular-strip boundary with nonzero flux

q=3,K=11,L=12,a=1,b=2,P={a},Q={b}. Width-two b strip rows0,1,one a-hole at(0,0); a elsewhere. Auxiliary targets A=Zbar intersect N(a), B=Zbar intersect regular-strip orbit. phi1 sums over all targets in Nhat(S), not only edges of height<=Gamma.

Recorded check: Ground-state quantifiers and projected graph identities need excluded inputs

Same periodic fixed lattice model, distinct/non-distinct labels treated literally. For projection witness q=3,K=11,L=12; one 2-spin or two adjacent 2-spins in all-1 background.

Recorded check: Equation(D.8) has the target-set size instead of the trace-state-space size

Finite auxiliary cyclic chain uniform on Vbar; trace on unbarred Z; disjoint nonempty A,B subsets of Z. K>=11 admits interior two-adjacent-hole ladder-tree configurations outside A union B.

Recorded check: Arbitrary path indices, MH energy bound and gateway restriction require local corrections

Fixed finite periodic lattice, K,L>=11. Arbitrary directed path of lengthN, potentially with repeated local cycles. For MH minimum-energy example, width-one strip and one-site protuberance. AppendixC q=2; K11,L12 regular width-three strip and an interior spin flip.

repair.content:
Derive a consistent effective generator and solve -Qg=1 for each target; or retain hitting constants and separately derive rates. The present contradiction alone does not identify which of the three asserted components should be replaced.

Analyze the actual invariant measure of the printed rates, or explicitly change generator and rederive barrier/time scaling/prefactors. An exponential mixture cannot silently be read as a convex mixture of exponentials.

Exclude regular-strip boundary as well as N(S) from Lemma9.10's harmonicity domain. Use sum phi1=0 plus each phi1=O(exp(-Gamma beta)) and o(1) potential variation on each regular orbit. Fixed finite volume makes the total o(exp(-Gamma beta)).

Require distinct pair labels, a not in{b,c} and b!=c for three-label clauses. Require inputs outside N(a), equivalently Pi eta_i!=a, in the graph identities.

Replace factor by |Z|, or explicitly define and use a further trace on A union B with its capacity.

Use actual path lengthN throughout; replace minimum by maximum; retain a higher-energy remainder in AppendixC's final equality.
